summary: CRT error-code mapper: stores the input OS error code a1 into the TLS slot returned by TLSOffsetGetter_afd8 (the _doserrno slot), then searches the DWORD-pair table starting at unk_5E65C0 and bounded by dword_5E6728 (error-code column at each entry, errno value at entry +4). On an exact match it writes the mapped errno via TLSOffsetGetter and returns the TLS pointer. On no match it applies range fallbacks: 0x13..0x24 -> errno 13, 0xBC..0xCA -> errno 8, otherwise errno 22, each written through TLSOffsetGetter.

operations.description: Call TLSOffsetGetter_afd8() and store a1 (the input OS error code) into the returned TLS slot, preserving the original code before mapping.
Scan the DWORD-pair lookup table: start v2 at unk_5E65C0 and advance two DWORDs per entry while v2 stays below the dword_5E6728 end bound, tracking the entry index in v1.
If the current entry's first DWORD (*v2, the error-code column) equals a1, the code is found in the table.
Call TLSOffsetGetter() and write dword_5E65C4[2 * v1] (the mapped errno, the entry +4 column of the matching row) into the returned TLS slot.
Return the TLS slot pointer written with the mapped errno on the table-match path.
If a1 is outside 0x13..0x24 and outside 0xBC..0xCA, call TLSOffsetGetter() and write errno 22 into the TLS slot.
If a1 is in 0xBC..0xCA, call TLSOffsetGetter() and write errno 8 into the TLS slot.
If a1 is in 0x13..0x24, call TLSOffsetGetter() and write errno 13 into the TLS slot.
Return the TLS slot pointer written on the range-fallback path.

unresolved: errno meanings of 13/8/22 come from existing analysis (EACCES, ENOEXEC-like, EINVAL); not independently verified within this packet.
The exact TLS slot semantics of TLSOffsetGetter vs TLSOffsetGetter_afd8 live in those callees, outside this function body.
